titulo: Work, forms and formal emails: E-mails formais e informais

aula.objetivo: Write formal and informal emails (greeting, subject, request, apology, closing), fill in forms and understand job and course ads, at A2 writing level.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: a formal email (to a company, to a stranger) opens with «Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren,» (or «Sehr geehrte Frau Müller,» / «Sehr geehrter Herr Müller,») and closes with «Mit freundlichen Grüßen» and the name. Use «Sie» and the polite forms. STEP 2: an informal email (to a friend) opens with «Liebe Anna,» or «Lieber Paul,» and closes with «Liebe Grüße» or «Viele Grüße». Use «du». STEP 3: the SUBJECT (Betreff) is short: «Anfrage zum Deutschkurs». STEP 4: the body follows: introduction, request, thanks: «Ich möchte mich für den Kurs anmelden. Könnten Sie mir bitte weitere Informationen schicken?» STEP 5: the FORMULA for a polite request: «Könnten Sie mir bitte …?», «Ich würde gern …», «Ich bitte um …». STEP 6: the reply: «Vielen Dank für Ihre Antwort.»
blocos.comparacao: English also has formal and informal openings («Dear Sir or Madam» / «Yours faithfully» versus “Hi Anna”), but German is more fixed: it has different greetings for formal («Sehr geehrte…») and informal («Liebe/Lieber…»), and uses Sie or du accordingly.

erros.motivo: In a formal email, the greeting is «Sehr geehrter/geehrte».
In German, the greeting is in German.

blocos.enunciado: Say out loud the opening and closing of a formal and of an informal email.
